author: kesudh
method: Independent cold construction from benchmark pins; versioned root-distance trees, fanout-aware congestion negotiation, exact per-net descent, fixed-work LNS, joint candidate selection and displacement chains. Every intermediate route is generated inside the same invocation. Each case records its actual producing source, seed and work counts.
hardware: ctrl/router: Intel Core i7-13700HX (16C/24T), 31.7 GiB RAM, Windows 11. int2float: existing GCE Intel Xeon 2.20 GHz VM, 4 vCPUs, 15.6 GiB RAM, Linux/Rust 1.90.0, nice19. Exact per-case hardware and platform are in runs.json.
route_inputs: Benchmark instance JSON only. All intermediate geometry is constructed in this invocation; no published routes, reference solutions, prior-entry routes or trained geometry artifacts.
runtime_scope: One complete solver process per case, including input parsing, cold construction, every internal refinement/portfolio phase, output serialization and process exit. Excludes compilation, pre-run instance copying and post-run official checking. Actual producing runs and times are retained when experiments do not improve them.
source: reproducers/<runs.json source_version>/router/src/main.rs under the shared intro entry
algorithm_credit: Search code adapted from kesudh earlier Rust engine; no geometry reused. Standard SPT, negotiated congestion and LNS; conflict splitting adapted from Sharon et al. Fanout-aware pricing and joint candidate selection informed by PathFinder/FastRoute literature and the public IrwinJam/m3d-router. New code independently implemented; no opponent code or routes copied.
configuration_policy: Each case runs.json solver_args and immutable source_version determine its exact producing configuration; CLI defaults do not replace those records.
